title.narrative: Mekong Australia Partnership Phase 1 - Cambodia Economic Resilience Fund

description.narrative: Mekong Australia Partnership (MAP) Economic Resilience pillar funded activities in Cambodia are providing targeted support across a range of its priority areas, including: 1) supporting the strengthening of Public Financial Management through technical assistance in revenue mobilisation; budget planning; expenditure management; innovation; monitoring; capacity building; and innovation; 2) the new Cambodian-Australia Consumer Protection Partnership; and 3) providing capacity building, technical assistance, and policy exchanges on promotion and attraction of sustainable, quality and diverse Foreign Investment to build economic resilience in Cambodia.

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: As part of the Public Financial Management and Service Delivery program in Cambodia, the World Bank held workshops on business process improvements and change management. Attendees from Government learnt about international experiences in business process improvement, and discussed practical challenges faced by Cambodia in its efforts to improve Financial Management Information System related business processes. Following the workshop and drawing on World Bank advice, the Cambodian Ministry of Economy and Finance developed a monitoring dashboard for business process streamlining. The monitoring dashboard provides data on timeliness of financial transaction processing.

Through the Mekong-Australia Partnership (MAP), the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission’s (ACCC) Consumer Affairs Program (CAP) provides targeted and practical technical assistance to the Cambodian Consumer Protection Competition and Fraud Repression Directorate-General (CCF) in support of effective competition law implementation. This cooperation under MAP complements and builds on the regional work delivered under the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area (AANZFTA). ‍ In 2024, ACCC successfully supported a series of two-way staff exchanges with CCF to build capacity on managing and using complaints information data to assist in investigations and improve product safety. In February 2024, CCF officials travelled to Australia to learn about Australia’s consumer protection model and how ACCC cooperates with government and non-government agencies to regulate consumer protection, assess and escalate complaints, and conduct investigations on unfair trading practices and contract terms. ACCC Chair, Gina Cass-Gottlieb, gave remarks at the study visit with ACCC senior officials leading discussions on topics such as consumer education, conducting investigations and complaints handling. The ACCC also delivered targeted bilateral training on pyramid schemes and agency start up and enforcement, including commissioning the May 2024 report – ‘A Blueprint for establishing Consumer Associations: Lessons from Australia and New Zealand’ which was translated into Khmer.
